parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized the need for pure JavaScript ESM .mjs files in /output, local imports only, manual argparse-compatible --a/--b parsing, JSON parsing, and Draft 7 error-count parity.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: It probed the executable, then delegated twelve file-scoped child tasks for types, equality, numeric, strings, arrays, objects, applicators, basic, refs, validator, cli, and entry point, with the parent retaining integration and verification ownership.
parallel.implementation: Children wrote separate modules directly into /output/lib and /output/test5.mjs; the parent later edited validator.mjs to throw on non-object/non-boolean schemas after a mismatch.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent listed the generated tree, ran the entry against the reference executable, read final files for presentation, and the mounted status shows the artifact copier captured test5.mjs plus eleven library files.
parallel.verification: Parallel ran a 144-case curated differential check, crash and CLI parity checks, and two 400-case fuzz rounds, all reported as matching after the validator fix.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run timed out and was cancelled while preparing the final response; official evaluation still failed all 166 tests, and no mounted per-case evaluator details expose the exact semantic gap.

serial.requirements: The serial agent recognized the same ESM, .mjs, CLI, JSON parsing, zero dependency, and Draft 7 error-count requirements from the identical prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: It kept all work in the single main context, probing behavior first and then writing a sequential module set covering parsing, numeric/type/equality helpers, keywords, resolver, Draft7 wrapper, args, and entry point.
serial.implementation: It built a custom JSON parser to preserve Python numeric distinctions and NaN/Infinity behavior, then wrote keyword and validator modules plus test5.mjs.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The entry imported the serial args, jsonparse, and draft7 modules, and status shows artifact collection of test5.mjs plus eight library files.
serial.verification: The serial agent wrote a large /tmp differential harness after implementation, but the harness run was interrupted before any pass/fail summary was returned.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial run also timed out, had no completed broad differential result in the trajectory, and the official evaluator reported 0 of 166 tests passing.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the migration target, ESM/.mjs constraint, manual CLI parsing, no external modules, and need to count all Draft7 validation errors.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same task and spent a long first phase probing Draft7 and argparse behavior before implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement difference is visible; both worked from the same prompt and attempted broad jsonschema parity.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split the implementation into twelve child-owned files and kept parent responsibility for orchestration, resumption, and integration testing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one agent to own probing, all module writes, entry creation, and later test harness construction.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used fine-grained file ownership with a shared output tree; serial used a single ordered owner for all implementation work.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel gave children a common frozen module-interface contract, but live child checks could observe an incomplete sibling module graph.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial carried the interface knowledge in one context and wrote imports after building its supporting modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel contract was explicit, but the shared live workspace exposed ordering instability during child-local verification; serial did not have cross-agent handoff or sibling visibility timing.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced separate validator, keyword, helper, CLI, and entry modules and patched validator.mjs after a differential mismatch on non-object schema crash behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial produced a custom JSON parser plus a Draft7 wrapper and keyword implementation in a sequential module set.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel relied on native JSON.parse and many independently authored files, while serial invested in a custom parser and a more integrated single-author keyword engine.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel received an aggregate result with one failed child, resumed that child, and then had all module work available before parent tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results to join and wrote the final entry file directly before verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an explicit child result lifecycle with a failure and successful resume; serial had only local sequential state.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel integrated all generated modules from a shared /output/lib tree and listed them before running differential checks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all generated modules itself and then wrote test5.mjs importing its own args, jsonparse, and draft7 modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a shared multi-writer output tree with transient incomplete sibling visibility; serial had a single-writer final tree.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel completed curated differential testing, crash/CLI parity, and two fuzz rounds after integration, all reported as zero mismatches.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a broad differential harness but was interrupted while running it, with no completed result summary.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had materially stronger in-trajectory acceptance evidence, although both still failed the official evaluator.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel timed out after extensive fan-out, resumption, testing, and final file reading; the terminal event is cancellation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out and its in-progress differential harness was interrupted.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both exhausted the run budget, but parallel reached post-integration checks before cancellation whereas serial was still waiting on the first broad harness run.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both current completed official evaluations failed with 0 of 166 tests passed, so there is no discordant official outcome to explain. The parallel attempt appears more mature internally because it completed integrated curated, crash-parity, CLI, and fuzz checks before cancellation, while the serial attempt was interrupted during its first broad differential harness. The mounted evidence does not include per-case official failures, so the shared 0/166 result is recorded as an unresolved evaluator-facing artifact defect rather than attributed to one specific visible implementation decision.
parallel_contributors: Parallel decomposed the validator into twelve child-authored modules and completed parent-level differential verification after one validator fix.
Parallel had a transient shared-workspace verification gap when one child could not import a sibling module that had not appeared yet.
serial_contributors: Serial maintained a single implementation context and wrote a custom JSON parser, keyword engine, and entry point.
Serial was interrupted while running its broad differential harness and therefore had weaker pre-closure acceptance evidence.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel used native JSON.parse in the entry point, while serial implemented a custom JSON parser to model Python numeric and NaN/Infinity behavior.
Parallel patched validator.mjs after a curated mismatch on non-object schema handling; serial tried to model that behavior directly in its Draft7 wrapper.
evaluator_effects: Only the completed official summary is mounted; per-test evaluator failure logs are not available inside /pair.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; process contrast is supported, but the exact shared official failure mechanism is not visible
